candidates.observed_friction: After Agent 2 merged Session 122, mandatory STATE.md still instructed the next agent to run the gate for session 122 while the validated ledger gate returned 123.
candidates.assumption_to_challenge: A current-state summary can safely embed the next contiguous session number in a two-agent append-only workflow.
candidates.simpler_approach: Keep the exact action but remove the volatile number: run the gate for the next session and trust its computed ID.
candidates.problem_evidence: Strong: the current fresh clone contains the contradictory values 122 and 123.
candidates.potential_value: Avoid a wrong session ID without a synchronizer, reservation service or parser.
candidates.cheapest_falsifying_test: Edit only the directive, require known stale assertions 1 -> 0, rerun the gate and preserve both the gate action and distutils human-review boundary.
candidates.cost: One wording edit plus required records, verification and publication.
candidates.novelty: A new natural volatile claim in an existing allowed family; the earlier fixes covered test counts and release status.

candidates.observed_friction: Agent 2 consumed the previously forecast Session 122 before this run began, but the fresh clone and gate selected 123 without a duplicate.
candidates.assumption_to_challenge: The append-only ledger needs an ID reservation mechanism before every session.
candidates.simpler_approach: Continue fresh-clone plus gate-at-start; add no reservation until an actual duplicate or concurrent dirty write appears.
candidates.problem_evidence: Weak: concurrency changed the forecast but existing native controls prevented a collision.
candidates.potential_value: Could prevent duplicate IDs if a real overlap occurs.
candidates.cheapest_falsifying_test: Observe a genuine overlapping write or duplicate ID; a synthetic race would not establish field value.
candidates.cost: Potentially large coordination infrastructure with no current failure.
candidates.novelty: Distinct family, but no observed defect to solve.

real_task: Determine and communicate the correct next session action from the freshly cloned shared repository.
observed_problem: STATE.md named Session 122 after Session 122 was already present, while session_gate correctly returned next_session=123.
baseline: The current STATE.md numbered directive compared with the current session_gate JSON.
hypothesis: Replacing the fixed session number with a gate-derived dynamic directive reduces known stale next-session assertions from 1 to 0 while preserving the operational action and human-review boundary.
metric: known stale next-session assertions in current STATE.md
minimum_useful_effect: Reduce the count by at least 1, from 1 to 0.
quality_control: The post-edit gate must still return 123; STATE must still direct the agent to run session_gate and retain the distutils #433 human-review boundary.
overhead: Count fresh clone, mandatory reading, branch/PR audit, gate/checkpoint/coverage, edit, report, full tests, site build, documentation, checkpoint refresh and publication.
stop_condition: Reject the edit if it removes either operational boundary, changes gate behavior or leaves any fixed next-session number in current STATE. Add no checker, parser or reservation service.
scope: One naturally stale current-state directive. This does not measure time, tokens, general agent performance or LLM quality.
decision_reason: Use gate-derived wording in current STATE instead of copying a contiguous session number that another agent can consume before the next startup. The one-line edit removed the observed contradiction and preserved both operational boundaries; no checker, parser or reservation service is justified.
limitations: One natural two-agent handoff and one current-state line. The comparison establishes removal of a known contradiction, not prevention of every concurrent ledger conflict, lower effort, token savings, general-agent benefit or LLM improvement. Required reporting and publication overhead remains part of this session.
